$comment: Riftlight authored opening draft. Development preview only; see ../README.md. Production campaign id will be riftlight. No bonus XP: preserve the design bible campaign budget.
title: A Way Back Uphill

plate.narration: A griffin leans over the ridge and lowers a rope ladder. Its bottom rung swings above the rising water. Up on the rocks, a dry path winds toward the pass. Time to climb.

goal.text: Find a dry way back uphill toward the mountain pass.

steps.label: Set the ladder on firm ground

bank.narration: You crawl onto the east bank under Frostfang, wet to the whiskers. High above, the broken shelf hangs like a bitten cracker. Behind you the river is climbing the stones, one pebble at a time. A griffin on a low ridge has been watching. "I am Tamsin! I keep the river line for the aerie," she calls. "The path to the pass starts up here, but the water is rising. Are all of you here? I can lower a ladder." Tonight you need a dry way back uphill, toward the mountain pass called the Cairnstep.

choices.label: Show her everyone is safe

count.narration: "Good!" calls Tamsin. "Stay right there. My ladder is stuck under a rock, and I need a minute to free it." The water licks at your boots. A minute is not long. Your rope is wet and tangled, and your packs are sitting right where the river wants them. What comes first?

choices.label: Wring out the rope and coil it
Carry the packs above the waterline

count_rope.narration: You squeeze the rope and pick the swollen knots loose with your thumbs. A tiny silver fish flips out of a loop and flops back into the river. It looks offended. Soon the rope sits in a neat coil, like a sleeping snake that has decided to be friendly.

choices.label: Look up at Tamsin

count_packs.narration: You carry the packs up to a flat rock, one by one, and line them up like sleepy dogs. One pack goes glug when you lift it. You pour out a cupful of river and one very confused pebble. Now nothing can float away if the water climbs another step.

choices.label: Look up at Tamsin

help.narration: Tamsin's ladder pops free. She lowers the rope ladder down the cliff, and its bottom rung swings just above the water. "I can hold the top, but I cannot fix the bottom," she calls. "If the foot is not on firm ground, the first climber will swing like the clapper in a bell. Can you settle it?"

choices.label: Move the ladder to firmer ground
Lash the ladder's foot to a boulder
Use brace to hold the ladder steady
Use smash to set the foot on the rock

ladder.narration: You and your friends take hold of the foot of the ladder. It is heavier than it looks, and the wet rope is slippery as a fish. A flat dry rock sits a few steps up the shingle. "On three," Tamsin calls from above. "One, two, and heave!"

choices.label: Heave together

haul_foot.prompt: Everyone grab the foot of the ladder and heave it onto the flat rock together.

onSuccess.narration: The foot slides onto the flat rock with a crunch, and every one of you was pulling.

onFailure.narration: The foot slips back and the bottom rung bumps your shins. You settle for a rock that is only mostly dry.

lash_foot.prompt: Tie the ladder's foot to the boulder with a knot that will hold.
lash_foot.narration: You take the free end of your rope and loop it around a boulder. There are a great many knots in the world, and you know a few of them. One of them might even be useful.

onSuccess.narration: The knot pulls tight, and the foot of the ladder stops swinging.

onFailure.narration: The knot is a clumsy lump, but it holds the foot to the boulder. The ladder will wobble a bit.

brace_foot.prompt: Use brace to hold the ladder steady while the team sets its foot. The hero with brace helps; choose who leads the lift.
brace_foot.narration: A thornguard knows how to stand firm so a friend can lean on them. That is what brace is for. One of you plants both feet on the shingle and holds the foot of the ladder still, while the rest of the party walks it onto the flat rock.

onSuccess.narration: The foot settles on the rock like a hen on an egg.

onFailure.narration: The foot settles, but with a wobble. It will have to do.

smash_foot.prompt: Use smash to lift the ladder's foot onto the rock. The hero with smash helps; choose who leads the team.
smash_foot.narration: A bigfoot can lift enormous things. That is what smash is for. One of you scoops up the foot of the ladder like a loaf of bread, and the rest of the party guides it to the flat rock.

onSuccess.narration: The foot lands on the rock with a thump that shakes the pebbles.

onFailure.narration: The foot lands a bit crooked. It will have to do.

foot_set.narration: The foot of the ladder stands on the flat rock and does not wobble at all. Tamsin tests it with one claw and gives a happy squawk. "Now it is a real ladder," she says. "Before anyone climbs, let us find the driest way up. Dry feet should find dry ground."

choices.label: Look for the driest way

variants.text: The foot of the ladder stands on the rock, but it wobbles when Tamsin tests it with one claw. "It will do for careful climbers," she says. "Before anyone climbs, let us find the driest way up. Dry feet should find dry ground."

scout.narration: The cliff above the shore is a puzzle. Some rock is dry. Some rock drips. A few cracks look like paths, then stop at nothing. "The aerie knows one easy line and one hard line that looks easy," says Tamsin. "Find me the easy one."

choices.label: Study the cliff for the driest line
Follow the small hoof prints in the mud

scout_cliff.prompt: Read the cliff and find the line with the fewest wet rocks.
scout_cliff.narration: You look at the cliff one crack at a time. Some cracks are dry and some are drippy. One has a pebble stuck in it that looks like a nose.

onSuccess.narration: You find it: a ledge, a crack, and a narrow track that zigzags up the scree. It is not for climbers, but somebody has used it a lot.

onFailure.narration: You pick a wet line by mistake and slide down a body length. A narrow track beside it is the one you wanted. You find it on the way down.

scout_prints.prompt: Follow the hoof prints through the mud without slipping.
scout_prints.narration: The mud is covered with little prints, shaped like two-toed hearts. They come down the shore in a hurry. Some of them are very small.

onSuccess.narration: You hop from firm patch to firm patch, and the prints lead you to the foot of a narrow track.

onFailure.narration: The mud grabs your boot, and you sit down hard. From down there, you see the prints much better.

scout_done.narration: A narrow goat track zigzags up the scree beside the cliff. At the bottom, the hoof prints leave it and run straight to the river's edge. They do not come back. Somewhere out on the water, you hear a very small bell.

choices.label: See what the river left on the shore

driftline.narration: The river really has tipped out its pockets. There is driftwood in heaps, one lonely boot, and a big net of hay tied up in yeti knots. The net bobs at the water's edge, ready to float away again. "Hay for the herd!" says Tamsin. "It came from upstream. If it floats off now, it is gone for good."

choices.label: Hook the net with a driftwood pole
Wade in and drag the net out
Lasso the net with your coiled rope

net_hook.prompt: Hook the net with the pole and draw it in.
net_hook.narration: You pick a long driftwood pole with a fork at one end, like a giant finger. The net keeps bobbing just out of reach.

onSuccess.narration: The fork catches a knot, and the net glides in like a sleepy seal.

onFailure.narration: The pole slips and the net spins away. You snatch a few bundles of hay out of the spray, which is better than none.

net_drag.prompt: Drag the heavy net out of the river together.
net_drag.narration: You wade in up to your knees and grab the knots. The net is full of water and does not want to leave the river.

onSuccess.narration: The net comes out with a great slurp, and you all fall over in the gravel. The hay is safe.

onFailure.narration: The river wins the tug of war. You save only one end of the net, with a few bundles of hay inside.

net_lasso.prompt: Lasso the net and pull it in with the dry coil.
net_lasso.narration: Your rope is coiled and ready. You twirl the loop once, twice, and let it fly.

onSuccess.narration: The loop drops over the net like a hat on a head. You haul it in, and the hay is safe.

onFailure.narration: The loop lands a little short. You reel in only one end of the net, with a few bundles inside.

net_saved.narration: Whatever hay you have smells of sweet grass and wet wool. As you gather it, you hear the little bell again, and this time you see where it is. Out on a gravel bar in the river stand three snowhorn goats, huddled together, with the smallest one in the middle. "The herd's," says Tamsin. "They came down the grazing route before the water cut it off. They will not swim, and I cannot carry a goat." A small pouch has come loose from the net's knots. It holds five coins. Tamsin drops a supper bundle down to you. "For the goats, or for you," she says.

choices.label: Look at the gravel bar

bar.narration: The gravel bar sits in the middle of a brown stream that was not there this morning. It is knee deep and quick. The goats stare at you. The smallest one sneezes. How will you reach them?

choices.label: Wade across on a rope line, all together
Lay flat stones as stepping stones
Use skyward or glide to carry a rope across
Use leap to jump the stream with a rope

bar_wade.prompt: Everyone grip the rope and wade across the stream together.
bar_wade.narration: You tie one end of the rope around the nearest big rock, and everyone takes hold. The water is cold enough to make your teeth sing.

onSuccess.narration: You climb out on the gravel dripping and cheering. Nobody let go.

onFailure.narration: A hidden hole dunks you to the middle. You all come up sputtering, still holding the rope.

bar_stones.prompt: Lay a path of flat stones across the stream, one at a time.
bar_stones.narration: Flat stones lie all over the shore, like dropped plates. You pick the biggest ones and look for the shallow spots.

onSuccess.narration: Stone by stone, the path grows. The last one lands on the bar with a clack.

onFailure.narration: One stone rocks and tips you in. You finish the path wet to the knees.

bar_fly.prompt: Use skyward or glide to carry a rope across the stream. The hero with wings helps; choose who leads.
bar_fly.narration: A griffin can fly up and read a river from above. A dragonling can glide over water the party cannot walk through. One way or the other, a rope goes over the stream, and the rest of you follow it.

onSuccess.narration: The line sags, then tightens. The rest of you cross it hand over hand.

onFailure.narration: The line sags too low, and everyone gets a wet ride across the middle.

bar_leap.prompt: Use leap to jump the stream with a rope. The hero with leap helps; choose who leads.
bar_leap.narration: A manticore can cross a gap in a single bound, with a rope held in its teeth. One bound is all it takes.

onSuccess.narration: One big bound, and the rope is across. The rest of you cross it hand over hand.

onFailure.narration: The bound lands short in the shallows, but the rope still reaches. You cross it with wet boots.

bar_reached.narration: You stand on the gravel bar, and the goats lean away from you, all horns and worry. The biggest goat has a cracked horn and a very disapproving face. The smallest wears a tiny bell on a faded ribbon, and the bell jingles every time it shivers. They are cold, wet and cross. They will not take one step into that water for strangers.

choices.label: Think how to bring them over

goats.narration: Three cold goats, one quick stream, and a rope line you built yourselves. The biggest goat stamps. The smallest goat jingles. How will you bring them over?

choices.label: Walk them over, one friend to each goat
Carry the smallest goat first
Use mend on the smallest goat's sore knee
Use a songkeeper's lullaby to calm them
Tempt them across with the supper bundle

goat_line.prompt: Everyone take a goat by the ruff and walk it across, nice and slow.
goat_line.narration: Each goat gets a friend. You hold a woolly ruff in one hand and the rope in the other. The goats plant their hooves like small, hairy anchors.

onSuccess.narration: Hoof by hoof, the goats come across. The biggest goat even looks pleased about it.

onFailure.narration: The goats balk halfway and splash everybody. They get across in the end, by pushing past you.

goat_carry.prompt: The strongest of you carries the smallest goat over the rope line.
goat_carry.narration: The smallest goat weighs about as much as a wet sack of potatoes, and it wriggles. The strongest of you hoists it onto a shoulder. The other goats watch very closely.

onSuccess.narration: The little goat jingles all the way across. The big goats follow their baby into the water, grumbling.

onFailure.narration: The little goat squirms and the carrier slips. A splash, a squawk, and two wet heads pop up. The big goats come anyway, to rescue their baby.

goat_mend.prompt: Use mend on the smallest goat's sore knee. The hero with mend helps; choose who leads.
goat_mend.narration: A unicorn has a gentle touch that makes a scrape stop stinging. It lays a hoof on the little goat's sore knee, and the big goats watch with their ears up.

onSuccess.narration: The little goat stands on its mended knee and trots into the water. The big goats follow, ears forward.

onFailure.narration: The knee feels better, but the goats still hate the water. They cross with a lot of complaining.

goat_song.prompt: Use a lullaby to calm the goats. The songkeeper helps; choose who leads.
goat_song.narration: A songkeeper hums a slow tune that sounds like a blanket. The smallest goat stops jingling. The biggest goat sits down to listen.

onSuccess.narration: The song rolls over the water. One by one the goats stop stamping and follow the tune across.

onFailure.narration: The song is lovely, but the stream is loud. The goats cross anyway, slowly, with their eyes shut.

goat_bait.prompt: Hold out the supper and lead the goats across, one sniff at a time.
goat_bait.narration: Goats will go anywhere for bread and cheese. You unwrap the supper bundle, and three heads turn at once. Three noses begin to twitch.

onSuccess.narration: The goats follow the smell across the stream like a very hairy parade. The biggest one gets the crust.

onFailure.narration: The goats lunge for the bundle, splash everyone, and eat it on the shore. They get across, which was the point.

goat_back.narration: The goats scramble up the shingle and shake themselves like dogs, spraying everybody. The smallest goat sneezes on the ladder. The biggest goat stamps twice, which seems to mean thank you. "There," says Tamsin. "Now the herd has all its horns again."

choices.label: Hear what Tamsin needs next

variants.text: Then the biggest goat spots the hay and goes straight for it, which is a very goat thing to do.

waterline.narration: Tamsin hops from rock to rock. "One more favor, while the goats chew. The aerie keeps a record of the river line, the place the water reaches. I need a marker at today's edge, so the keepers can tell how fast it climbs." She flaps toward a tall flat rock. "Stones, please, and a steady paw."

choices.label: Stack a cairn of stones at the water's edge
Scratch a line into the cliff with a sharp stone

stack_cairn.prompt: Whoever has the steadiest hands stacks the stones, and the others pass them up.
stack_cairn.narration: You choose the flattest stones and build from the bottom. Big stones go first and small ones go last. A pebble goes on top, because the top is where a pebble belongs.

onSuccess.narration: The cairn rises, stone on stone, taller than your knee. It does not tip.

onFailure.narration: The cairn leans, wobbles, and falls with a clatter. You stack a shorter, fatter one that stays.

scratch_line.prompt: Find the water's edge and scratch a clear line above it.
scratch_line.narration: You pick a sharp stone and look at the cliff. The wet stripe on the rock shows where the river has been. A line goes right above that.

onSuccess.narration: The line comes out clean and straight, with a small arrow under it. Tamsin reads it from the ridge.

onFailure.narration: The first line comes out crooked. You scratch another beside it, and Tamsin reads both.

waterline_done.narration: Tamsin squints at your mark and nods slowly, the way griffins nod when they are pleased and trying not to show it. "Tomorrow the water will be higher," she says. "Then the keepers will know how fast the river climbs. A river with a number on it is half tamed."

choices.label: Rub your cold hands together

fire.narration: The goats are shivering, and so are you. Tamsin points to the lee of a big rock, out of the wind. "Nobody climbs my ladder with stiff fingers," she says. "Cold rungs are slippery rungs." Driftwood lies all around, but it is as wet as everything else. How will you warm up?

choices.label: Build a fire in the lee of the big rock
Huddle with the goats and rub everyone dry
Use smash to split a log into dry kindling

fire_build.prompt: Find dry wood, shelter the spark, and light a fire.
fire_build.narration: Wet wood will not light, but the inside of a log is often dry. You break the thickest pieces open. Out come little curls of dry wood, like shavings.

onSuccess.narration: A tiny flame catches, grows, and crackles. Every face turns toward it.

onFailure.narration: The first spark fizzles, and so does the second. In the end you get a smoky, grumpy fire that warms you a little.

fire_huddle.prompt: Rub the goats and each other dry, and share the warmth.
fire_huddle.narration: You do not need a fire to get warm. You press in close and rub everybody down with a handful of hay and your own sleeves.

onSuccess.narration: Goats are surprisingly hot. Soon everyone is toasty, and the smallest goat is asleep on a boot.

onFailure.narration: Everyone gets rubbed a bit dry and stays a bit damp. It is the thought that warms you.

fire_smash.prompt: Use smash to split a log into dry kindling. The hero with smash helps; choose who leads.
fire_smash.narration: A bigfoot can break a barrier or lift something enormous. One whack on a log, and out spill dry splinters from the middle.

onSuccess.narration: The log cracks open like a nut, and the dry heart of it lights at the first spark.

onFailure.narration: The log splits into big, damp lumps. You get a smoky fire that warms you a little.

rest_fire.narration: For a few minutes, the shore is cozy. Steam rises from the goats. Steam rises from your socks too, and one sock smells like river pudding. Tamsin watches from her perch with her head on one side. The next thing to do is climb, but nobody has to hurry yet.

choices.label: Dry your socks by the warm
Ask Tamsin about the aerie
Share a bite of supper with Tamsin and the goats

rest_socks.narration: You hang your socks on a stick, and they steam like little flags. The smallest goat eats the corner of one, thoughtfully, and then spits it out. The biggest goat leans on you, warm and damp, and you feel like a very large pillow. It is nice for a minute.

choices.label: Get ready to climb

rest_share.narration: You break the supper into five fair bits, for goats do not like to be left out. Tamsin takes hers with great dignity and then gets cheese in her feathers. Pleased, she digs in her saddle bag and pulls out a bright singing-day ribbon. "The aerie wears these on feast days," she says. "Wear it for luck."

choices.label: Get ready to climb

rest_story.narration: "Our aerie is above the ridge," says Tamsin. "We keep a pass ledger, a big book of every road through the peaks. Our keeper writes down each new path and each path that closes. This season there is a path in the ledger that was not there before, and he cannot decide whether to believe it." She ruffles her wings. "He needs someone to walk it. You are walking the right way."

choices.label: Get ready to climb

surge.narration: A crack like a giant's knuckle splits the air upriver. A slab of broken shelf has dropped into the water. A brown wave rolls down the shore, fast, with foam on top like a bad hat. "Ladder! Now!" shouts Tamsin. The goats see the goat track before you do, and they are already running for it.

choices.label: Run for the ladder, all together
Boost the goats onto their track, then follow
Use roar to keep everyone moving
Use brace to hold the line against the wave

surge_run.prompt: Everyone run for the ladder before the wave arrives.
surge_run.narration: You run for the foot of the ladder with the wave behind you. The wet shingle slides under your boots like marbles.

onSuccess.narration: You reach the ladder as the wave slaps the rocks behind you. Nobody is swept off.

onFailure.narration: The wave catches your heels and sloshes you against the cliff. You grab the rungs and hold on.

surge_chain.prompt: Everyone lift a goat onto the goat track, then jump after it.
surge_chain.narration: Goats are quick on scree, but the first step is steep. You boost them onto the track one rump at a time.

onSuccess.narration: The last hoof leaves the shingle just as the wave arrives. The goats bound up the track like they own it.

onFailure.narration: The wave soaks your boots as you shove the last goat up. It looks back at you with deep reproach.

surge_roar.prompt: Use roar to keep everyone moving. The hero with roar helps; choose who leads.
surge_roar.narration: A manticore can make a very loud noise at exactly the right moment. The roar rolls along the shore, and every goat and friend begins to run.

onSuccess.narration: Everybody hears the roar, and nobody argues with it. You are at the ladder before the wave is.

onFailure.narration: The roar is loud, but the wave is louder. You get wet to the knees before the rungs.

surge_brace.prompt: Use brace to hold the line against the wave. The hero with brace helps; choose who leads.
surge_brace.narration: A thornguard knows how to stand in front so friends can run behind. One digs in at the foot of the ladder and takes the first slap of the wave.

onSuccess.narration: The wave hits the braced line and splits around it. Everyone gets to the ladder with dry elbows.

onFailure.narration: The wave is bigger than it looked. The line holds, but everyone gets a shove and a splash.

surge_after.narration: The wave breaks around the foot of the ladder, which does not move at all. Tamsin lets out a long breath. The goats trot up the track and out of sight. The water settles into a steady, bossy flow a full body length higher, right over the stones where you stood a minute ago.

choices.label: Look up the long ladder

variants.text: The wave slams the foot of the ladder and swings it hard. Tamsin hangs on to the top with both claws, feathers flying. The ladder wobbles back into place. The goats trot up the track and out of sight. The water settles into a steady, bossy flow a full body length higher, right over the stones where you stood a minute ago.

ascend.narration: The ladder is long and the rungs are wet. Above you, Tamsin leans over the edge, and above her is the ridge. The goats are already up there, looking down, as goats do. How will you climb?

choices.label: Climb in a line, each friend steadying the next
Haul the packs up on the rope first, then climb light
Use skyward or glide to carry the packs up
Use rally to cheer on tired climbers

climb_line.prompt: Climb the swaying ladder in a line, each friend steadying the next.
climb_line.narration: You put the lightest climber in front and the strongest at the bottom. Everyone holds the rung ahead and the rope beside it.

onSuccess.narration: Hand over hand, rung by rung, the line climbs. The ladder sways, and so do your stomachs, but nobody lets go.

onFailure.narration: A rung slips under a boot, and the line swings like a conga line. Everyone hangs on and climbs the rest with shaky knees.

climb_sling.prompt: Haul the packs up on the rope, then climb with free hands.
climb_sling.narration: Packs are heavy on a ladder, and wet packs are heavier. You tie them to the rope in a big bundle for Tamsin to haul.

onSuccess.narration: The packs go up in a swinging bundle, and Tamsin catches them one by one. Then you climb with nothing but yourselves.

onFailure.narration: The bundle swings into the cliff with a bonk, and a pack opens. You catch your things as you climb.

climb_wings.prompt: Use skyward or glide to carry the packs up. The hero with wings helps; choose who leads.
climb_wings.narration: Wings are good for more than flying yourself. A griffin or a dragonling carries the packs up in short hops, and the rest of the party climbs with free hands.

onSuccess.narration: The packs float up in a few quick flights, and then you climb with free hands.

onFailure.narration: A pack slips and falls with a splash, and then you fish it out. It is a bit wetter than before.

climb_rally.prompt: Use rally to cheer on tired climbers. The songkeeper helps; choose who leads.
climb_rally.narration: A songkeeper can lift a friend who is down. A quick climbing song, and tired arms find some spring in them.

onSuccess.narration: A bright rally goes up the ladder, and every climber finds an extra rung of energy.

onFailure.narration: The rally is cheerful, but the rungs are still wet. You get to the top with sore arms.

top.narration: You haul yourself over the edge and lie on the rock, panting. The ridge is dry. Really dry! Tamsin sits beside you, grinning with her whole beak. Along the ridge, a narrow dry path winds toward a notch in the peaks, with stacked stones lining it like stairs. "The Cairnstep," she says. "The keeper at the pass is a griffin called Brask. He keeps the ledger, and he has more ink on his feathers than on the page."

choices.label: Pull up the rope and look at the ladder

safety.narration: Tamsin peers over the edge at the ladder. "One more thing, and then I will let you go. The river will be up again tomorrow, and the next travelers will be wetter and more tired than you. A ladder is good. A ladder with a handrail is better." She drops the end of a long rope beside you. "Where should it be tied?"

choices.label: Tie the handrail to the old boulder
Wedge a driftwood peg into the crack and tie to that
Buy an iron peg from Tamsin for 3 coins

safety_boulder.prompt: Tie the handrail to the boulder with a knot that will hold a tired traveler.
safety_boulder.narration: The old boulder at the top of the ladder is as wide as a table and as steady as a hill. It has been waiting a very long time for someone to tie a rope to it.

onSuccess.narration: The knot is round, fat and neat. Tamsin tugs it with all her weight and it does not budge.

onFailure.narration: The knot slips on the first tug. You tie it again, a bigger one this time, and it holds well enough for careful hands.

safety_peg.prompt: Everyone pull on the peg to make sure it will not slip.
safety_peg.narration: You find a thick stick of driftwood and hammer it into a crack with a rock. Thunk, thunk, thunk. Then you tie the rope around it.

onSuccess.narration: The peg bites the crack and stays put, even when all of you hang off the rope. Tamsin looks impressed.

onFailure.narration: The peg creaks and shifts. You wedge in a second one beside it, and then it holds.

safety_buy.narration: Tamsin keeps a sack of iron pegs for just this, and the aerie sells them for a few coins to buy ink. You pay, and she drops the best peg into your hand. It is cold and heavy and rings like a bell. You hammer it deep into the rock, and the rope on it feels as steady as a hill.

choices.label: Tie off the rope

safety_done.narration: The rope hangs beside the ladder, tight and straight. Tamsin tests it with one claw, then leans on it with her whole chest, which is a lot of griffin. "Better for the next travelers too," she says. "Somebody will thank you in the dark, and they will not even know your names." She hands you a smooth river charm on a cord. "The aerie gives one to anyone who ties a rail."

choices.label: Ask what Tamsin will tell the keeper

word.narration: Tamsin shakes the water off her wings. "I must stay by the ladder, because more people may come out of that river. But Brask should hear about it from someone who was there. Which news should reach him first?"

choices.label: The river is still climbing
The herd's route is cut, and its goats were stranded

word_river.narration: Tamsin nods slowly. "The river line, yes. If it climbs again tonight, the whole east bank goes under, and so does the old path along it." She scratches a small mark on her wing feather. "I will send the news up on the wind, and Brask will have it before you do."

choices.label: Take the dry path

word_goats.narration: Tamsin nods slowly. "The herd's route, yes. The ledger has a line for it. It is a short line, but it matters." She scratches a small mark on her wing feather. "I will send the news up on the wind, and Brask will have it before you do."

choices.label: Take the dry path

climb.narration: The dry path leads away along the ridge, under the peaks of Frostfang. At the end of it, a line of stacked stones climbs toward a notch. Behind you the river mutters, and the ladder sways. You are dry, you are together, and the goats are on their way home. Your rope and packs are still with you. The Cairnstep is next.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
